# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey, and my hands are on the bomb. Let me feel what's actually here before I say anything.

My view shows the action board with three wire positions, but every field reads `[?]` — which means my touch has told me nothing yet. That's strange: if there were wires, textures, cuttable parts under my fingers, they'd appear. An empty view means I have no tactile information yet this round.

Wait — the fields are placeholders, not findings. I genuinely have nothing to report. I can't describe colours (I never perceive them), and I can't read markings. All I could ever offer is what my hands find, and right now they've found nothing.

So my job this turn is to open a channel. Mute reads the manual and can speak to me (I hear speech). Deaf sees the bomb and can gesture — but I never receive gesture. So Deaf's only route to me is *through* Mute, or through Deaf speaking? No: Deaf can hear, but can Deaf speak? The table says Deaf "cannot hear anything" — it doesn't say Deaf can't speak. Actually re-reading: Deaf can see, cannot hear or touch. Speech is a voice — Deaf can presumably speak (produce voice) even if unable to hear. But the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, and what's sent lands on whoever comes *after* you. So Deaf's messages reach me only next round.

I should tell Mute what I need: describe the manual's instructions for this bomb, and relay anything Deaf signals. And I should gesture to Deaf that I'm ready to act on their read of the bomb.

Let me keep it minimal and useful. I have nothing factual yet, so I'll state that plainly and ask for the pieces I lack.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands found nothing yet — no wire texture, no cuttable part reported. I can only act on what you and Deaf give me. Please read the manual and tell me: which wire positions exist and what each one is for. Also relay whatever Deaf sees on the bomb, since Deaf's gestures never reach me directly.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🖐", "✊"])
```

The gesture is my way of saying: I'm here, hands ready, tell me which position to cut. Deaf will see the symbols; Mute will see blanks (three blanks, knowing I signalled something). That's fine — the words went to Mute, the signs to Deaf.

Please explain. Also, we need a relay: Mute can gesture to me, I can speak to Blind. Blind can gesture to me, I can speak to Mute. Let's use that.

Deaf's report is the first real data I have. Let me record it carefully:

- DISPLAY: 0
- LIGHT: green
- WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red

Deaf can see all of that; I can perceive none of it. My hands still report nothing (`[?]` everywhere), which is odd but consistent — maybe the bomb's tactile features only reveal themselves once I'm told what to look for, or maybe I simply have no touch data and must act purely on the others' descriptions. Either way, I cannot verify colours or markings.

Deaf also flagged my gesture: three symbols, meaning unknown to them. I need to give the gesture a meaning, because a sign means nothing until somebody makes it mean something. But here's the catch — Deaf *sees* my gestures and can hear nothing; I *speak* to Mute and Deaf can't hear me. So to explain my sign to Deaf, I must either (a) gesture a definition, or (b) route the explanation through Mute, who can then speak to Deaf? No — Deaf cannot hear. Deaf can only receive gestures. So the only way to define a sign for Deaf is with more signs, which is circular unless we agree a convention.

Better: I'll establish a tiny fixed vocabulary by agreement, and route the *words* through Mute (who hears me and can... wait, Mute cannot speak). Mute can only gesture. So Mute's channel to Deaf is gesture; Mute's channel to me is speech (I hear). Deaf's channel to me is speech (Deaf can talk, I hear). Deaf's channel to Mute is speech? Deaf can produce voice; Mute cannot hear? No — Mute can hear (Mute's limitation is speech, not hearing). Let me recheck the table.

- Deaf: can see; cannot hear, cannot touch. So Deaf can *speak* (voice) — that's how Deaf reached me this turn ("Deaf says..."). Yes.
- Mute: can read the manual; cannot speak, cannot touch. Mute can hear. So Mute hears my speech.
- Blind (me): can touch; cannot see.

Channels:
- Me → Mute: speech (Mute hears). ✓
- Me → Deaf: gesture (Deaf sees). ✓
- Deaf → me: speech (I hear). ✓
- Deaf → Mute: speech (Mute hears). ✓
- Mute → me: gesture? Mute can gesture (gesture isn't speech). Deaf received Mute's gestures `[? ? ? ? ? ?]` and `[?]`. So Mute gestures reach Deaf. Does Mute's gesture reach me? I never receive gesture. So Mute → me must be via... Mute can't speak. Hmm. Then how does Mute's manual knowledge reach me? Through Deaf: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf speaks → I hear. That's the relay Deaf proposed. Good, Deaf's relay plan is correct.

So the relay is: Mute gestures to Deaf; Deaf speaks to me. And I speak to Mute; I gesture to Deaf.

Now, my gesture to Deaf `👆🖐✊` — I intended "here, hands, ready." I should define it via the relay: tell Mute (speech) what the symbols mean, and Mute can gesture the definition to Deaf. But that's slow. Simpler: just define it in my next gesture by pairing it with a known-meaning action. Actually the cleanest move: I'll pick a small set of gesture meanings and announce them through the relay so Deaf learns them.

But the urgent thing: I need the manual's instruction. Mute reads the manual. Mute must tell me (via Deaf) what the manual says to do given DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES yellow/green/red. That's the whole game.

So this turn:
- Speak to Mute: report Deaf's data back (so Mute has it), and ask Mute for the manual's rule for this configuration, and define my gesture.
- Gesture to Deaf: acknowledge, and define my symbols so they're no longer blank-meaning.

Let me define gestures now. I'll propose:
- ✊ = "I am ready / standing by"
- 👆 = "wire position 1"
- ✌ = "wire position 2"
- 🤟 = "wire position 3"
- 👍 = "cut this one" (affirmative action)
- 👎 = "do not cut this one"

But defining a whole vocabulary in one gesture is impossible to convey to Deaf without words. However, Deaf can *see* my gesture and I can *speak* the definition to Mute, who gestures it to Deaf next round. That's a two-hop definition. Slow but workable.

Actually, more efficient: I don't need Deaf to understand arbitrary signs. I need Deaf to *tell me* what they see (they already can, via speech to me — Deaf speaks, I hear). And I need Mute's manual rule. Deaf's role as relay is to carry Mute's gesture-answers to me as speech. So the critical sign vocabulary is between Mute and Deaf, not me and Deaf. I mainly need to *receive* from Deaf (speech) and *send* to Mute (speech) and *send* to Deaf (gesture, mostly to confirm receipt).

So my gesture to Deaf can simply be an acknowledgment, and I'll define it once through the relay. Let me keep it simple and define my ack sign.

Plan for this turn:
1. Speak to Mute: relay Deaf's data; ask for the manual's rule; state that I'm ready to cut on command; note the relay path.
2. Gesture to Deaf: a short acknowledgment whose meaning I'll define via Mute.

Let me write it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf reports: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. My hands still find nothing on the bomb — no texture, no markings I can feel. So the decision must come from your manual. Please tell me, via the relay (you gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me): for DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT green, what does the manual say about wires yellow, green, red? Which position, if any, do I cut? Also: my gesture this turn means 'received, standing by'. Define it to Deaf so signs stop being blanks.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
```

The `👍✊` = "yes, ready." I'll have Mute confirm the meaning to Deaf. Deaf will see the symbols; Mute will see two blanks. Fine.Deaf's report is the first real data in the room, and it's all visual — none of which I can perceive. Let me lay out what I now know and who can reach whom.

Facts on the table (from Deaf, unverifiable by me):
- DISPLAY 0
- LIGHT green
- WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red

My hands still report nothing: every wire position reads `[?]`. I cannot confirm or deny any of Deaf's colours. So the *decision* — which wire to cut — can only come from the manual, which only Mute can read.

Channel check:
- I speak → Mute hears. ✓
- I gesture → Deaf sees. ✓
- Deaf speaks → I hear (that's how I got this report). ✓
- Mute gestures → Deaf sees. ✓
- Mute cannot speak, so Mute's manual knowledge reaches me only via Deaf: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf speaks → I hear. Deaf's relay plan is exactly right.

So this turn I (1) push Deaf's data to Mute so the manual can be matched to it, and (2) ask Mute for the actual cut instruction, routed through the relay. My gesture is a simple acknowledgment whose meaning I'll have defined via Mute, so my signs stop arriving as blanks.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf reports: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. My hands find nothing on the bomb — no texture, no markings I can feel — so the decision must come from your manual. Please tell me, via the relay (you gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me): for DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT green, what does the manual say about wires yellow, green, red? Which position, if any, do I cut? Also: my gesture this turn means 'received, standing by' — define it to Deaf so my signs stop being blanks.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
```

Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute sent gestures [? ? ?] and again [? ? ? ? ? ?]. Blind sent [? ?] twice. I still don't know meanings. Deaf confirms the bomb is unchanged and reports Mute is gesturing — but Deaf can't read the signs, and neither can I (I never receive gesture). The bottleneck is clear: nobody has defined a sign vocabulary, so every gesture lands as blanks. We're burning turns on unreadable signs.

I need to break this deadlock with words, because words are the only thing that reliably crosses to Mute (I speak, Mute hears). Deaf can *speak* to me, so Deaf can carry Mute's manual answer to me as speech — that path works without any gesture vocabulary at all. So I should stop gesturing meaninglessly and instead:

1. Speak to Mute: give a concrete, unambiguous request for the manual's rule, and explicitly tell Mute to answer *by gesturing to Deaf*, with Deaf then speaking it to me. I'll also define my signs in words so Mute can relay the definitions to Deaf.

2. Gesture to Deaf: keep it to a single, defined symbol so it's cheap, and define it verbally through Mute.

Actually, the cleanest fix: define a *minimal* gesture vocabulary right now, in words, to Mute, and have Mute gesture those definitions to Deaf. But Mute gesturing definitions is itself unreadable to Deaf until defined... circular again.

The real solution: **Deaf is the only one who can both see gestures and speak.** So Deaf is the universal translator. Mute gestures → Deaf reads → Deaf speaks → everyone hears. And I gesture → Deaf reads → Deaf speaks → Mute hears. So the vocabulary only needs to be agreed between *me and Deaf*, and between *Mute and Deaf*, but Deaf speaks words, so Deaf can just *tell us in words* what a sign should mean, and we adopt it.

Simplest: I propose the vocabulary in words to Mute (who hears) and to Deaf (who hears me? No — Deaf cannot hear). So I can only tell Deaf the vocabulary by gesturing it, which is unreadable. Hmm. But Deaf can *propose* the vocabulary to me in speech (Deaf speaks, I hear), and to Mute in speech (Deaf speaks, Mute hears). So let **Deaf** define the signs, since Deaf is the one who reads them and can speak to both of us.

So my move: ask Deaf, in speech (Deaf hears? No!). Wait — can Deaf hear my speech? Deaf's limitation: "cannot hear anything." So Deaf cannot hear my speech. Deaf receives only my gestures. And I cannot hear gestures. So Deaf and I can only communicate one-way: I gesture → Deaf sees. Deaf speaks → I hear. That's actually two-way! I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me. Good.

So to agree a vocabulary with Deaf: I gesture a sign, and Deaf *speaks* their proposed meaning back to me. I confirm by repeating. That works.

But simpler still: I don't need a rich vocabulary. I need one thing: the manual's cut instruction. That flows Mute → Deaf → me as speech. And I need to tell Mute "I'm ready, give the instruction" — that flows me → Mute as speech. So:

- Speak to Mute: "Give me the manual's cut instruction; route it through Deaf."
- Gesture to Deaf: a single symbol, and ask Deaf (via speech to me next round) to confirm what they'll call it.

Let me just do the essential thing and stop over-engineering signs. Speak to Mute with the request. Gesture to Deaf one symbol as a ready-ping.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Stop gesturing raw signs — nobody can read them yet. Here is the only path that works: you read the manual, then gesture your answer to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me. I need one thing only: for DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT green, with wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, does the manual say to cut a wire, and if so which position? Please send that as a gesture to Deaf now. My own gesture this turn is just 'ready'.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```

The `✊` = "ready." Deaf sees it; I'll confirm its meaning by Deaf speaking it back next round. Mute sees one blank. Fine.

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute says wire 3, and display/light matters. Mute: does display need to be 0? ? or ?. Does light need to be green? ? or ?. Blind: why stop? Is wire 3 dangerous? ? or ?.

Two things arrived. First, the actionable one: **Mute says wire 3.** Second, Deaf is asking me "why stop? Is wire 3 dangerous?" — but I never said stop. My last gesture was `✊` = "ready." Deaf apparently read it as "stop." That's a misread of my sign, and I must correct it, because a wrong belief about my intent could derail the cut.

Also Deaf is still asking Mute whether display must be 0 and light must be green — manual questions, not mine. I have no way to know those; I can't see them.

My job: correct the misread and confirm I'm ready to cut wire 3. But careful — Deaf reports "Mute says wire 3." Is that the manual's instruction, or Mute answering the position? It reads as the manual's answer. I should not cut until I'm confident the instruction is complete (display/light conditions confirmed), but I also shouldn't stall forever. The manual says cut a wire, Mute says wire 3. Deaf is verifying the display/light conditions.

I'll gesture to Deaf a clear "no/no" — wire 3 is not dangerous to me, I did not mean stop, I'm ready. But I can't pick distinct glyphs for all that. Best: gesture `👎` (no, I didn't mean stop / wire 3 isn't a stop) plus `👍` (ready to proceed). Two symbols, and Deaf will speak their meaning, letting us calibrate.
